title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document consolidates company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and managers to ensure consistent, secure, and auditable practices across Redwood Inference.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors interacting with company systems and data. Exceptions must be documented and approved per the Exception Handling section below.

1) Access & Permissions

Purpose: define RBAC principles, access request and approval workflows, periodic review cadence, and escalation paths.

Principles
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access (RBAC) with clearly defined role templates for common job families (engineering, SRE, finance, people-ops, sales).
- Separation of duties for sensitive actions (e.g., production deploys, billing changes, key management).

Common roles and owners
- IT Admin (people-ops): owner of identity provider (IdP) configuration and onboarding templates.
- SRE: owner of production deploy roles and runbook access.
- Security: owner of privilege review process and approval for elevated rights.

Access request workflow (standard)
1. User completes Access Request form (internal template: /templates/access-request).
2. Manager approves for business justification.
3. Role owner (team lead) approves.
4. IT/Identity team provisions access and documents request ID.
5. Automated email to requester and manager with expiry (default 90 days for temporary privileges).

Elevated access (production, crypto keys, billing)
- Requires two approvers: direct manager + Security on-call.
- All actions must be recorded in audit logging (CloudIAM audit logs, identity-provider audit events).

Periodic review
- Quarterly automated reviews for all roles with access to production and billing.
- Teams must re-affirm member lists via the Access Review dashboard in Redwood Console.

Emergency access
- Emergency access must be requested via the Emergency Access runbook. Approval from SRE lead and Security manager is required post-facto within 24 hours for retrospective audit.

2) Change Management

Purpose: ensure safe, auditable changes to infrastructure and services while balancing velocity.

Change types and approval matrix
- Standard changes (low risk, pre-authorized): automated deploys covered by CI/CD guardrails (no manual approval).
- Normal changes (non-standard, scheduled): require change request (CR) submission, manager approval, and scheduling in the maintenance calendar.
- Emergency changes: follow Emergency Change procedure (see below).

Change windows and scheduling
- Weekly deploy freeze windows: none by default; teams coordinate via team calendars.
- Production Change Window (recommended): 02:00-06:00 UTC for disruptive maintenance unless approved otherwise.

Change request process (normal)
1. Submit CR using /templates/change-request (include rollback plan, owner, impact, test plan).
2. Engineering manager and SRE review for capacity/contingency.
3. Security review if change touches secrets, IAM, or networking.
4. Schedule deploy and notify stakeholders at least 48 hours prior.

Emergency change procedure
- Trigger: active outage or critical vulnerability.
- Steps: 1) Initiate Emergency CR, 2) Notify Incident Commander, 3) Execute change, 4) Post-change verification, 5) Postmortem and retrospective within 5 business days.

Rollback and validation
- Every CR must include a rollback plan and post-deploy validation checklist (smoke tests, key trace metrics).

3) Data Management

Purpose: protect customer and company data through classification, handling, retention, and secure disposal.

Data classification
- Public: non-sensitive, safe for public release.
- Internal: internal business information; limited distribution.
- Confidential: customer data, contracts, financials; requires encryption at rest and in transit.
- Restricted: regulated data (e.g., PII, PCI, HIPAA) - special handling and legal review required.

Handling and storage requirements
- Confidential and Restricted data must be stored in approved repositories only (S3 buckets with encryption and IAM policies, approved database clusters).
- Keys: Customer and production encryption keys must be managed via KMS/HSM (integrations: AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault).
- Backups: Daily backups for production DBs, weekly full snapshot retention for 90 days, and monthly archival retention for 1 year unless legal retention dictates otherwise.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention for logs: 90 days hot, 365 days cold; sensitive audit logs retained for 3 years.
- Data deletion: use documented Deletion Request template and verify deletion via tool-generated proof (S3 object lifecycle, DB redaction logs).

Data access reviews and DLP
- Quarterly data access audit driven by Security.
- DLP rules enforced on email and file sharing for Confidential/Restricted classifications.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Purpose: provide clear thresholds and steps for purchasing goods, software, and travel, and for employee expense reimbursement.

Approval thresholds
- <$1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,000- $50,000: Manager + Finance (procurement review).
- >$50,000: VP-level approval + Procurement + Legal (contract review).

Procurement process (software and hardware)
1. Requestor fills the Purchase Request form (/templates/purchase-request) with business justification and cost center.
2. Manager approves and forwards to Procurement team.
3. Procurement obtains quotes (minimum 2 vendors preferred for >$10k).
4. Finance validates budget; Legal reviews contract for >$50k or if vendor will store customer data.
5. PO issued and order tracked in Redwood Purchasing system (RPS).

Expense reimbursement
- Employees should use the Expense Report template (/templates/expense-report).
- Receipts required for all expenses over $25.
- Reimbursement timeline: Finance processes weekly; expect payment within 14 days of submission.

Corporate card usage
- Corporate cards issued by Finance; misuse is subject to disciplinary action and card revocation.

Travel booking and per-diems (summary)
- Preferred travel vendors listed in /procurement/travel-vendors.
- Use economy fares for domestic travel; premium economy allowed for flights >8 hours with Manager pre-approval.

5) Vendor Management

Purpose: ensure vendors are onboarded, assessed for risk, and managed through contract lifecycle and renewals.

Onboarding checklist
- Vendor Assessment form completed (/templates/vendor-assessment).
- Security questionnaire (standard or SOC2/ISO proof) and penetration testing requirements if vendor handles Restricted data.
- Contract template completed by Legal with appropriate SLAs, liability caps, and data protection clauses.

Risk tiers and controls
- Low: SaaS tools with no customer data - standard contract, annual review.
- Medium: vendors processing internal/confidential data - encryption requirements, quarterly security attestations.
- High/Restricted: vendors storing customer or regulated data - require SOC2 Type II or equivalent, annual audits, and security onboarding call.

Renewal and offboarding
- Renewal checklist includes evidence of security posture, updated contract, and PO.
- Offboarding requires data return or verified deletion and revocation of all access (IdP, API keys, service accounts).

6) Travel Policies (detailed)

Booking and approvals
- All travel must be pre-approved via Travel Request template (/templates/travel-request).
- Managers must confirm business purpose and budget.

Safety and emergency support
- Traveler must register trip with People Ops travel tracker.
- Company provides emergency assistance contact (People Ops on-call).

Expense categories and limits
- Hotel: reasonable single occupancy rate; team leads may approve upgrades when justified.
- Meals: per diem guidance available in /templates/meal-allowances.

7) Internal Templates and Forms

Location: /templates (consolidated list). Key templates included as attachments or links: 
- access-request.json (Access Request)
- change-request.md (Change Request template)
- purchase-request.xlsx (Purchase Request)
- vendor-assessment.pdf (Vendor Assessment)
- expense-report.xlsx (Expense Report)
- travel-request.md (Travel Request)

8) Roles, Ownership, and Review Cadence

Owner summary
- People Ops: Access & Permissions, Travel, Corporate cards.
- Security: Data Management, vendor security assessments, DLP.
- Finance/Procurement: Procurement, expenses, vendor financial reviews.
- Eng/SRE: Change Management and deploy/runbook governance.

Review cadence
- Full policy review: annual (People Ops owns schedule).
- Critical controls (data, vendor security): quarterly review by Security.
- Procurement thresholds and templates: reviewed semi-annually by Finance and Legal.

9) Exceptions and Escalations

Documented exceptions must include justification, compensating controls, and an expiration date. Exception owner is responsible for tracking and remediation. Escalation path: Team Lead -> Department Head -> Chief Legal Officer / CTO as appropriate.

10) Audit and Evidence Requirements

- Access requests, approvals, and provisioning logs must be retained for a minimum of 3 years.
- Change requests and rollout evidence retained for 2 years.
- Vendor contracts and assessment evidence retained for contract life + 3 years.

Appendix A - Quick reference tables

Approval thresholds table:
| Item | Approver(s) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <$1,000 purchases | Manager | Auto-approve if in budget |
| $1k- $50k purchases | Manager + Finance | Procurement involved for >$10k |
| >$50k purchases | VP + Procurement + Legal | SLA/contract review required |

Retention summary:
- Logs: 90d hot / 365d cold
- Sensitive audit logs: 3 years
- Backups: daily, 90-day primary retention, monthly archives 1 year

Appendix B - Example commands and links
- Grant access (IdP CLI example): idpctl grant --user alice --role deployer --expiry 90d
- Revoke API key (example): vault token revoke <token-id>
- Change request template: /templates/change-request

Contact and feedback
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Security contact: security@redwood.ai
- Finance/Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
